mechanism_narrative: Because TRANSIT and WORKPLACES are still well below baseline and both improved only modestly from t-3w to t-0w, the city is in a slow-recovery commuting regime that should continue to lift discretionary shopping visits over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not average above its last-4-week mean while TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain below baseline and do not deteriorate sharply, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: The jump in GROCERY_PHARM to slightly above baseline at t-0w indicates more routine local errand activity; when that shift persists, nearby retail and recreation spending follows with a short lag as households combine errands with discretionary trips.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM crosses above 0 after being negative in the prior week
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not rise within one week after GROCERY_PHARM stays at or above baseline, the mechanism is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in PARKS and RESIDENTIAL, especially when parks usage is improving while time at home remains elevated, implies more local leisure and neighborhood circulation that redirects spending to nearby retail venues over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises week-on-week while RESIDENTIAL stays above +10
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC fails to improve over the following two weeks when PARKS rises and RESIDENTIAL remains above +10, the interaction claim is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT falls further below its already depressed level, the resulting mobility frictions suppress access to retail districts and should push RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT declines below -25 after having been above -23 in the prior week
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not fall relative to the prior four-week average after TRANSIT crosses below -25, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A positive gap between RESIDENTIAL and WORKPLACES means more people are staying home while commuting activity weakens, which reduces spontaneous retail trips and should depress RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL exceeds WORKPLACES by at least 20 points
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not weaken within two weeks when RESIDENTIAL is at least 20 points above WORKPLACES, the mechanism fails.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS remain deeply negative but begin to recover from a recent trough, the implied improvement in outdoor leisure activity should spill over into mall and high-street visits with a lag of roughly one month.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises for two consecutive weeks after being below -18
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC is not higher over the next 28 days after PARKS posts two straight weekly gains from below -18, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A combined rebound in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES signals fuller weekday circulation into the city center; once both series improve together, retail-and-recreation mobility should increase within one week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both rise week-on-week
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not rise within one week after simultaneous gains in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: In a post-restriction reopening regime, falling reliance on RESIDENTIAL mobility and stabilizing transit should unlock shopping trips, making RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks than over the previous four.
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC remains below its prior four-week mean despite residential time easing and transit stabilizing, the mechanism is rejected.
